banner.subTitle: I specialize in Java and C#, bringing over six years of experience building high-volume enterprise systems across both backend and frontend architecture.

aboutMe.title: My goals!
aboutMe.content:
With over **6 years of experience** architecting, building, and supporting high-concurrency enterprise applications and distributed backend systems, including nearly three years engineering mission-critical systems for Latin America’s largest investment bank.

My core technical expertise spans both the **C#/.NET** and **Java/Spring Boot ecosystems**, alongside full-stack capabilities in React, cloud infrastructure (AWS and Azure), and advanced database optimization (PostgreSQL and MS SQL Server). Throughout my career, my primary focus has been translating complex business bottlenecks into resilient, high-throughput software. At BTG Pactual, I architected a digital onboarding workflow for an asset management platform handling millions of requests per minute, reducing customer processing times from 2 days to 2 hours while doubling overall document throughput.

Holds a **Postgraduate Diploma in Software Architecture** and a **BSc in Software Engineering**, I approach system design with a rigorous focus on clean architecture, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), automated test coverage using SonarQube, and proactive observability using Datadog. I actively incorporate AI-assisted engineering workflows (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, and Agentic AI frameworks) to accelerate development delivery while ensuring all AI-generated code meets strict quality, performance, and security gates.

Currently based in Limerick, Ireland, I relocated to expand my international reach and immerse myself in the European tech landscape. I am driven by complex engineering challenges, technical mentorship, and building software that delivers measurable enterprise value.

itens.title: 🏓 Pong a Classic, Reimagined
itens.brief: A browser-based take on the arcade classic. Rally against the computer, chase the score, and see how long you can keep the ball in play.
itens.description:
A browser-based take on the arcade classic. Rally against the computer, chase the score, and see how long you can keep the ball in play.

## ✨ Features

- Player-versus-computer gameplay
- Live score tracking
- Paddle and scoring sound effects
- Spoken score announcements
- Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and [p5.js](https://p5js.org/)

## 🎮 How to Play

Move your mouse vertically to control **Player 1’s paddle**. The computer controls the opposite paddle. Keep the ball in play and score by getting it past your opponent.

## 🚀 Run Locally

1. Clone or download this repository.
2. Open `index.html` in a browser, or serve the project with a local development server.
3. Move your mouse over the game to play.

> The game loads p5.js and p5.sound from CDNs, so an internet connection is needed.

## 🗂️ Project Structure

- `index.html` — Page markup and game score display
- `index.css` — Game layout and styles
- `sketch.js` — Game logic, paddles, ball, scoring, and audio
- `images/` — Game artwork
- `sounds/` — Sound effects

## 🛠️ Built With

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- p5.js

---

Have fun rallying! 🏓

itens.title: 👋 Automated CI/CD Jenkins
itens.brief: A small REST API that says 'hello' and a simple example of building, testing, packaging
itens.description:
Simple example of building, testing, packaging, and publishing a Java application with Jenkins and Docker.

## ✨ What It Does

The Spring Boot app exposes two greeting endpoints:
 
 - `GET` - `/greeting` (`Hello World. This application is UP with Jenkins.)`
 - `GET` - `/greeting/jenkins` (`Hello World. I am automated with Jenkins.)` 

## 🛠️ Built With

- Java 17
- Spring Boot 3.4.3
- Maven
- Docker
- Jenkins

## 🚀 Run Locally

 **Prerequisites**

- Java 17
- Maven, or use the included Maven Wrapper

 **Build and test**

On macOS/Linux:

```bash
./mvnw clean package
```

On Windows:

```powershell
.\mvnw.cmd clean package
```

Run the application:

```bash
java -jar target/greeting-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

The API will be available at `http://localhost:8080`.

Try the endpoints:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/greeting
curl http://localhost:8080/greeting/jenkins
```

## 🐳 Run with Docker

Build the application JAR first, then build and run the image from the repository root:

```bash
docker build -t greeting-app .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 greeting-app
```

Then visit `http://localhost:8080/greeting` or `http://localhost:8080/greeting/jenkins`.

## ⚙️ Jenkins Pipeline

The `Jenkinsfile` defines a pipeline that:

1. Checks out the `main` branch.
2. Builds the project with Maven.
3. Runs the Maven tests.
4. Builds and tags a Docker image.
5. Pushes the image tags to Docker Hub.

The pipeline expects a Jenkins Maven tool named `mvn`, Docker available on the build agent, and Docker Hub credentials configured in Jenkins with the ID `dockerHub`. The pipeline uses Windows `bat` steps, so its agent must support those commands.

> **Before running the pipeline:** replace the `TAG_VERSION` placeholder in the Docker build and push steps with the desired image version. The pipeline also publishes the `latest` tag.

## 🗂️ Project Structure

- `src/main/java/com/teteo/greeting/GreetingApplication.java` — Spring Boot application entry point
- `src/main/java/com/teteo/greeting/controller/GreetingController.java` — Greeting REST endpoints
- `src/main/resources/application.properties` — Application configuration
- `src/test/java/com/teteo/greeting/GreetingApplicationTests.java` — Application context test
- `Dockerfile` — Container image definition
- `Jenkinsfile` — Jenkins build and image-publishing pipeline
- `pom.xml` — Maven project and dependency configuration

---

A small app, from source code to a Docker image—with Jenkins automating the journey. 🚀

itens.title: 🍽️ AluraFood Microservices (back-end)
itens.brief: Distributed microservices and AWS CDK infrastructure. Explore a food-ordering backend built as a set of Java microservices and Java AWS CDK infrastructure
itens.description:
The project demonstrates service discovery, API routing, synchronous service calls, resilient communication, and asynchronous payment events with AWS infrastructure defined using CDK.

## 🧩 Architecture

- **Order** — handles order requests and uses MySQL.
- **Payments** — handles payment requests, uses PostgreSQL, and publishes payment-confirmation events.
- **Rating** — receives payment-confirmation events and handles ratings.
- **Eureka Server** — service registration and discovery.
- **Gateway** — entry point that routes requests to registered services.
- **RabbitMQ** — distributes payment-confirmation events.

The payment service publishes to the `fanout.payment.confirmation` exchange. The Order and Rating services each receive the event through their own queues.

## ✨ What You’ll Find

- Java 17 and Spring Boot microservices
- Spring Cloud Eureka service discovery and Gateway routing
- Synchronous communication with OpenFeign
- Resilience patterns with Resilience4j: circuit breaker, retry, and fallback
- Asynchronous messaging with RabbitMQ
- MySQL for orders and PostgreSQL for payments
- Flyway database migrations, Lombok, and ModelMapper
- Swagger/OpenAPI support
- AWS CDK definitions for VPC, ECS, Fargate, and RDS resources

## 🌐 Local Endpoints

Start the services and their dependencies before using these routes:

 
- Eureka dashboard | `http://localhost:8762/` 
- API Gateway | `http://localhost:8090` 
- Orders | `http://localhost:8090/order-ms/order` 
-  Payments | `http://localhost:8090/payments-ms/payment` 
- Ratings | `http://localhost:8090/rating-ms/rating` 
- RabbitMQ management | `http://localhost:15672/` 

## 🚀 Run Locally

### Prerequisites

- Java 17
- Docker with Docker Compose
- MySQL and PostgreSQL instances configured for the services

Database and service connection settings are in each service’s `src/main/resources` configuration files. Review those settings and provide credentials appropriate for your environment.

### Start RabbitMQ

From the repository root:

```bash
docker compose -f payments/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

### Build and test a service

Each Java service is a separate Maven project with its own wrapper. Run the following from the service’s directory, for example `Order`:

macOS/Linux:

```bash
./mvnw clean verify
```

Windows:

```powershell
.\mvnw.cmd clean verify
```

Repeat for `Server`, `gateway`, `payments`, and `rating` as needed.

### Start the application

Run each service in a separate terminal. Start Eureka first, then the Gateway and the application services. Make sure RabbitMQ and the configured databases are available. Once the services have registered with Eureka, send requests through the Gateway using the routes above.

## ☁️ AWS Infrastructure

The `alura-aws-infra` directory contains a Java AWS CDK project with infrastructure definitions for a VPC, ECS cluster, RDS, and a load-balanced Fargate service. Review the CDK code and your AWS account and region configuration before synthesizing or deploying. AWS resources may incur charges.

## 🗂️ Repository Structure

- `Order/` — Order microservice
- `payments/` — Payment microservice and RabbitMQ Compose configuration
- `rating/` — Rating microservice
- `Server/` — Eureka discovery server
- `gateway/` — Spring Cloud Gateway
- `alura-aws-infra/` — AWS CDK infrastructure project

---

A practical playground for exploring how distributed services communicate, recover, and scale. 🚀
